_doc: Spec DC-000: where recorded legacy behaviour differs from the independent contract oracle. Each entry is evidence for the owning spec to decide, not a fix. Changed only by a reviewed PR; test_legacy_characterisation.py fails if the computed set of divergences differs from this list in either direction.

divergences.note: Legacy lowercases units (except exact mW/MW) and strips whitespace, so this spelling is read as a power unit. HA's UnitOfPower spellings are exact; whether Nimbus accepts a miscased template-sensor unit is a contract decision. DC-002's resolver (device_bindings.py) takes the contract side and refuses it; the legacy readers are unchanged until DC-006.

Legacy reads lowercase 'mw' as megawatt, a documented choice in power_units.py (a milliwatt house sensor does not occur in practice). The contract refuses it as neither exact mW nor MW. DC-002's resolver (device_bindings.py) takes the contract side and refuses it; the legacy readers are unchanged until DC-006.

No unit: read as kW by design ('kW was always the assumption'). The contract treats a missing unit as unresolved rather than assumed. DC-002's resolver (device_bindings.py) takes the contract side and refuses it; the legacy readers are unchanged until DC-006.

No unit attribute: read as kW by design. The contract treats a missing unit as unresolved rather than assumed. DC-002's resolver (device_bindings.py) takes the contract side and refuses it; the legacy readers are unchanged until DC-006.

price_intervals.py's provider readers (_ordered) keep the first of two overlapping rows and drop the second, silently. The oracle refuses overlapping published intervals. DC-002's resolver refuses the whole series (reason overlapping_intervals); the legacy solver path is unchanged until DC-006.

price_intervals.on_grid holds the last interval's value at grid times past its end, flagging them real=False. The oracle never extends a price past its interval. DC-002's resolver reports the tail as a coverage gap with no value; the legacy solver path, which reads the flag, is unchanged until DC-006.

Mark Purcell, PR #1774: a price is $/kWh, $/MWh or c/kWh, scaled as required. price_intervals.price_unit_scale reads a price with no unit as $/kWh, as every price sensor always was. DC-002's resolver refuses it (unit_missing): a unitless number is not one of the three. The legacy readers are unchanged until DC-006.

Mark Purcell, PR #1774: a price is $/kWh, $/MWh or c/kWh. price_intervals.price_unit_scale also scales c/MWh (x 0.00001). DC-002's resolver accepts only the three units (plus the cent sign and the site currency code for $) and refuses c/MWh (unit_not_price). The legacy readers are unchanged until DC-006.
